Numbers just hit: July unemployment change 6k vs 5k expected Prior -1k July unemployment rate 6.4% vs 6.3% expected Prior 6.3% It points to some softness in labour market conditions in the summer with unemployment rising by 6k in July.

That brings the total number of unemployed persons recorded to roughly 2,993,000 people.

But perhaps the standout figure is the unexpected nudge up in the jobless rate, moving back up to 6.4%.

That is the highest since April, which at the time was the highest since July 2020.

So, that arguably points to softer conditions overall as economic conditions in Europe's largest economy remains benign at best since the turn of the year.

Naturally, the added struggles from the uncertainty caused by the Middle East conflict is not helping with the situation.

The German labour office notes that: "Unemployment and underemployment are rising noticeably in July, primarily due to seasonal factors.

Overall, the weak trend observed in the labour market over recent months is continuing." This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

CPI POSTCARD: EUROPEAN SESSION In the European session, the main highlight is the Eurozone Flash CPI report.

The headline CPI Y/Y is expected at 2.9% vs 2.8% prior, while the Core Y/Y measure is seen at 2.4% vs 2.4% prior.

The ECB will likely want to see benign inflation figures in this and the next report to hold off from raising interest rates at the next meeting in September.

In fact, in the usual post-meeting "leaks", the ECB signalled that it's ready to hike rates in September unless the inflation outlook improved markedly.

This means that the bar for a rate hike is low.

Better core inflation figures and a de-escalation in the Middle East is what the ECB is hoping for.

Right now, the market is pricing in a 68% chance of a rate hike in September with a total of 36 bps of tightening expected by year-end.
